Amberwood at Holland sells 11% of units on launch weekend, averaging $3,019 psf
article:
Sim Lian Group sold 23 of the 212 units, or 11%, at Amberwood at Holland over its launch weekend of Sept 25–26. The units were sold at an average price of about $3,019 psf.

However, based on the 70 units released in the first phase, the take-up rate was 33%, says Justin Quek, deputy group CEO of Realion (OrangeTee & ETC) Group.

With a unit mix comprising only three- to five-bedroom layouts, demand was primarily driven by owner-occupiers and families drawn to the project’s “spacious, family-centric designs and low-density exclusivity”, notes Quek.

Get the latest details on available units and prices for Amberwood At Holland

Of the 23 units sold, 11 were four-bedroom units, and nine were three-bedroom units, while the remaining three were five-bedroom units.

The three-bedroom units were sold at prices ranging from $2.516 million to $3.043 million, averaging $2,962 psf. The four-bedroom units sold for $3.111 million to $4.024 million, averaging $2,990 psf. Meanwhile, the five-bedroom units sold for $3.912 million to $4.834 million, averaging $3,026 psf.

The 23 units or 11% sold over the launch weekend is the lowest take-up recorded among CCR projects launched over the past 12 months. Dunearn House and Newport Residences each sold about 56% to 57% of their units at launch, while River Modern and Skye at Holland sold 90% and 99%, respectively (see table).

“Amid macroeconomic uncertainties, some homebuyers today may be taking a wait-and-see approach, or requiring more time to deliberate before making a purchase,” says Kelvin Fong, CEO of PropNex. “We see the sales performance as a measured start given that the project has no smaller units, which typically drive sales.”

In the first nine months of 2026, about 51% of units sold at the other three CCR launches during the period — Newport Residences, River Modern and Dunearn House — were priced below $2.5 million, based on URA Realis caveat data, according to PropNex Research.

Without one- and two-bedroom units, Amberwood’s entry price of $2.516 million is well above that of the other CCR launches over the past 12 months. One-bedroom units at Newport Residences started from almost $1.3 million, while a 527 sq ft compact two-bedroom unit at Dunearn House started from $1.48 million.

“Accordingly, with prices starting at around $2.5 million, the project has limited entry-level options,” says Fong. “While there has been continued interest in the project because of its exclusivity and location, the buyer pool is understandably narrower as many households tend to have budgets below $2.5 million.”

At an average price of $3,019 psf, Amberwood at Holland is priced below the other new CCR launches this year. River Modern averaged about $3,284 psf, while Newport Residences and Dunearn House averaged $3,162 psf and $3,133 psf, respectively, based on caveats lodged as at Sept 20.

“For buyers seeking 870 sq ft or more in the CCR, Amberwood at Holland is among the more competitively priced options in the market today,” notes Fong.

Realion’s Quek expects sales to pick up over time, citing the project’s proximity to King Albert Park MRT Station and schools such as Methodist Girls’ School and Pei Hwa Presbyterian Primary School, which are within 1km and 2km of the project, respectively.

Huttons Asia CEO Mark Yip says some buyers may also be assessing the implications of the recent change to the Phase 2C Primary 1 allocation rules, given Amberwood's positioning as a family-oriented development near popular schools.

Amberwood comprises 11 blocks of four to six storeys and offers only three-, four- and five-bedroom units. There are 74 three-bedroom units ranging from 872 to 980 sq ft, 74 four-bedroom units of 1,076 to 1,313 sq ft and 64 five-bedroom units of 1,335 to 1,572 sq ft. All residences have ceiling heights of 3.18m and come with V-ZUG appliances, Liebherr refrigerators and Villeroy & Boch sanitary ware.

It is the first private residential development in Holland Plain, a new residential precinct planned by URA in prime District 10. The precinct is set within the Good Class Bungalow enclaves of Brizay Park , Ewart Park and Garlick Avenue. Amberwood is also across the road from Holland Green Linear Park and adjacent to an upcoming park.

Sim Lian was awarded the Holland Link site in August 2025 after submitting the top bid of $368.37 million, or $1,432 psf per plot ratio (ppr).

In May 2026, Sim Lian was the sole bidder for the adjacent 99-year leasehold Holland Plain site, which it secured for $454 million, or $1,491 psf ppr. The site is expected to yield about 280 units and is slated for launch in 2Q2027.

ERA Singapore CEO Marcus Chu says buyers of larger, higher-quantum homes are taking more time to assess factors such as long-term liveability, practical layouts, location fundamentals and overall value before committing.
